text: Artificial Intelligence and the Board of Directors: AI Governance Frameworks and Disclosure Practices of Canadian-Listed Corporations presents the following source proposition: An empirical study of TSX-60 listed companies, based on regulatory filings and structured content analysis, reveals a significant gap between the widespread recognition of AI as a material risk factor and the formal integration of AI governance into corporate architecture. This proposition is pertinent to Kaal's source-bound claim that CIA provisions create economic incentives that affect directors' diligence, because stipulated daily noncompliance penalties stacked on top of monetary penalties under federal health laws expose companies that executed CIAs to significant financial ramifications.
